headline: Medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks arise from shared API/file surfaces and unverified handoff between plano and rasa.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: plano can ingest and route content via an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and config files, while rasa consumes conversational text from channels like Slack and Telegram. That creates a plausible handoff where attacker-controlled text from one side can be treated as instructions by the other. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF plano forwards raw model output into rasa channel messages without sanitization, injection is reachable.
IF rasa templates or policies parse upstream text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every cross-agent message.
Strip instruction-like prefixes before forwarding text.
Route only structured fields, not free text, between agents.
Review one sample end-to-end message path for prompt markers.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and broad network egress; rasa handles text and voice and connects to third-party messaging APIs. Even without a shared filesystem, a bridge that forwards conversation or telemetry can leak sensitive content from one agent into the other’s outbound channels. The interaction is undocumented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF logs or traces from plano are forwarded into rasa responses, sensitive operational data can leak.
IF rasa relays user text to external channels, any upstream secrets embedded in that text can be exposed.
mitigations: Disable forwarding of logs/traces into chat replies.
Mask secrets before any cross-agent transfer.
Limit rasa connectors to a test channel for one hour.
Inspect one outbound message template for embedded telemetry.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles lack multiple-instance support and neither advertises filesystem write, git, or database mutation. plano has broad egress and rasa has allowlisted egress, but the profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources. The main conflict surface is limited to coordination overhead, so this stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API scope, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator runs them concurrently against one shared queue, contention may appear.
mitigations: Assign separate queues for each agent.
Stagger runs by a few seconds.
Confirm no shared write target is configured.
Check whether either agent writes to the same webhook.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: plano can emit routed outputs through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and rasa’s dialogue-understanding subagent can consume conversational text. If rasa treats plano’s output as authoritative, a bad classification or hallucinated fact can cascade into downstream replies. There is no documented verification step, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF rasa uses plano-generated text as the final response draft, errors propagate downstream.
IF no human or rule-based verification sits between them, a mistaken upstream fact can be repeated.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before final replies.
Require citations for any factual claim passed across the bridge.
Compare one sample response against source text.
Disable auto-send for one test conversation.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating on forwarded outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch in the profiles. plano touches logs and traces, while rasa handles text and voice, but the evidence does not show a regulated-data flow or a jurisdictional conflict. Because the compliance pathway is unproven, this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents, a policy review is needed.
IF one deployment adds retention or residency constraints not shown here, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm whether regulated data is in scope.
Check retention settings on both deployments.
Document the data flow for one representative request.
Restrict the pair to non-regulated test data.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls.
